tldr:
For every public parameter tuple with nonempty \(\mathcal M_{\rho_0}\), the three-term scale
\[
r(n,N,\rho)=\max\left\{N^{-1/2},\min\bigl[n^{-s/(2s+d)},(n\rho^{d-m})^{-s/(2s+m)}\bigr],(nN)^{-s/(2s+d)}\right\},
\] with the radius-dependent source entry infinite at zero, is the uniform minimax absolute-risk and connected 90-percent-honest expected-length frontier over \(\rho\in[0,\rho_0]\). A public matrix-and-radius optimization selects a legal whole-range affine baseline from nonemptiness alone. Shrinking positive-volume graph cohorts force the collapse-specific source floor; a boundary-corrected observable estimator and public finite-sample certificate attain the frontier. On corrected noncollapsing graph slices the precision loss is polynomial. With \(\rho=n^{-\beta+o(1)}\), the source elbow is \(1/(2s+d)\), and the strict interaction window closes at the explicit \(\beta_*\), contrasting with the comparator elbow \(1/(2s+d-m)\).
gap: Fixed known-weight thin-set integration and the noncollapsing repository frontier do not control probability-normalized target cohorts whose positive graph volume approaches zero. A fixed normalized density envelope cannot substitute for a physical volume floor.
